title: Sugar and the Macula

patient.name: Mdm Siti Aishah
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for PAM before cataract surgery — diabetic with possible maculopathy

history.hpc: Mdm Siti says 'My sugar high for many years already, now my eye also blur.' She has a cataract and long-standing diabetes with possible diabetic maculopathy. The doctor ordered a PAM to estimate the potential vision before deciding on cataract surgery.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes for 15 years. Cataract. Possible diabetic maculopathy under review.

examination_findings.fundus: Doctor notes possible diabetic macular changes

pam.interpretation: A borderline predicted acuity suggests the diabetic maculopathy may partly limit the benefit; correlate with macular imaging

diagnosis: PAM completed after dilation, giving a borderline predicted acuity that suggests the diabetic maculopathy may partly limit the benefit of cataract surgery. The OT reports the result and recommends correlation with macular imaging; the OT does not make the surgical decision.

immediate: Confirm identity and the correct eye against the order
Explain the test and position the patient
Note the diabetic maculopathy as a relevant confounder
Record and report the result to the doctor
follow_up: Correlate with macular OCT / diabetic eye assessment
Doctor to counsel on realistic expectations given the maculopathy
patient_education: Explain the test estimates likely vision after the cataract is removed
Reassure that the diabetic eye will also be assessed
Explain dilation will blur near vision for a few hours

key_points: Confirms identity and the correct eye
Confirms dilation as required for PAM
Notes diabetes and possible maculopathy as relevant
Explains the purpose of the test
Understands PAM estimates the benefit of surgery
Links the borderline result to diabetic maculopathy
Does not make the surgical decision
Reports the result and confounder to the doctor
Documents the predicted acuity and diabetic history
